rule: Accounting reports the financial performance of a business.
trap: Reputation, environment and customer relations — real business concerns, not accounting.
tell: Financial performance is the only financial phrase in the set.

rule: It summarises cash from operating, investing and financing activities.
trap: Invented report names that sound plausible.
tell: Three activity categories name one statement.

rule: Employees care about the firm's ability to fund benefits.
trap: Competitors, vendors, suppliers — external parties with other concerns.
tell: Whose benefit is at stake?

rule: Following GAAP makes a company comparable to others.
trap: Tax and income effects. GAAP is about comparability, not reducing tax or income.
tell: GAAP standardises so statements can be compared.

rule: The PCAOB regulates audits of public companies.
trap: FASB sets standards; the IRS collects tax; peer CPA firms do not regulate.
tell: Public company audit oversight is one body.

rule: Information technology has changed accounting most.
trap: Narrower technology answers, and certification.
tell: The broadest technological cause.

rule: It shows ownership (equity) and debt (liabilities).
trap: Revenues, expenses and costs — all income statement items.
tell: Balance sheet is a position; income statement is a period.

rule: The residual interest in net assets.
trap: Liabilities and revenue definitions.
tell: Residual means what is left after debts.

rule: Assets = liabilities + owners' equity. $300M + $100M = $400M.
trap: Arithmetic near-misses at $50M intervals.
tell: Add the two right-hand terms; do not subtract.

rule: Revenue is recognised when the service is performed, not when cash moves.
trap: Cash collected before or after the service, and signed contracts.
tell: Find the year the work was done.

rule: Cash to and from owners and creditors.
trap: Investing and operating categories, plus an invented one.
tell: Owners and lenders means financing.

rule: Significant accounting policies live in the notes.
trap: The three statements themselves.
tell: Policies are disclosed, not tabulated.

rule: An audit gives assurance that statements fairly present financial position.
trap: Predictions about credit, income or cash flow. An audit never predicts.
tell: Fairly presents, not will perform.

rule: Verifiability, relevance, materiality and conservatism, matched to their definitions.
trap: Definitions that sound alike; each maps to exactly one term.
tell: Match on the distinguishing word in each definition.

rule: The scored order: prepare statements, analyse them, gather information, make the decision, implement it.
trap: The intuitive order — gather first — which is the trap here.
tell: Statements are the starting input, not the output.

rule: Current assets divided by current liabilities.
trap: Ratios built from total assets or the wrong denominator.
tell: Current over current. Both words must match.

rule: Debt ratio over 100% means liabilities exceed total assets.
trap: The same number measured against sales, net income, or current assets.
tell: Debt ratio is total liabilities over total assets.

rule: If COGS is a constant percentage of sales, falling gross profit means falling sales.
trap: Expenses below the gross profit line — salaries, interest, tax.
tell: Gross profit is only sales minus COGS.

rule: Adequacy above 1 means operating cash covers commitments; a cash cow is well above 1.
trap: Ratios below 1, which look similar in size.
tell: Divide before comparing. Only two exceed 1 comfortably.

rule: Cash before interest and taxes divided by cash paid for interest.
trap: The same numerator over taxes, operations or acquisitions.
tell: Interest earned means interest in the denominator.

rule: Obligations due beyond one year.
trap: Items due in weeks or months, which are current.
tell: Twelve months is the line.

rule: Buying equipment with cash: equipment up, cash down.
trap: Entries that touch equity or debt when neither changed.
tell: One asset up, one asset down. Equity is untouched.

rule: Paying insurance in advance creates an asset: prepaid insurance up, cash down.
trap: Equity or payable entries.
tell: Paid in advance means an asset, not an expense yet.

rule: Operating expenses and ordinary gains and losses affect net income.
trap: Dividends and stockholder contributions — equity transactions, not income.
tell: Owners' transactions never touch net income.

rule: It shows gross profit and income from operations as subtotals.
trap: Balance sheet lines.
tell: Subtotals of a statement of performance, not of position.

rule: Under accrual, cost is recognised when the goods are received, not paid for.
trap: The month of payment or of sale.
tell: Match the expense to the event, not the cash.

rule: Cost less salvage, divided by life, times the months held.
trap: Full-year amounts, or the wrong month count.
tell: Count the months actually owned.

rule: Services delivered on credit: receivables up, and retained earnings up by the revenue earned.
trap: Retained earnings moved by the cash amount rather than the revenue.
tell: Revenue earned drives equity; cash timing does not.

rule: Divide the projected figure by one plus the growth rate to get the base year.
trap: Multiplying instead of dividing, which inflates the base.
tell: Work backwards from the projection.

rule: Operating, investing, financing.
trap: Marketing, production and planning — business functions, not cash categories.
tell: Only three categories exist.

rule: Cash received from investors is financing.
trap: Investing, which is about buying and selling assets.
tell: Money from owners is financing, not investing.

rule: Buying plant assets is investing.
trap: Dividends and stock issuance, which are financing or operating.
tell: Investing means long-term assets.

rule: Selling equipment increases cash from investing.
trap: Operating, which is where the gain on sale appears but not the proceeds.
tell: The asset sold decides the category, not the profit on it.

rule: The indirect method is more common among large US companies.
trap: The direct method, or equal popularity.
tell: Indirect starts from net income and is easier to prepare.

rule: Cash in from customers less cash out for operating items.
trap: Totals that include an investing or financing line.
tell: Include only operating receipts and payments.

rule: An error is unintentional: a miscalculation, or an unintentional misclassification.
trap: Theft and auditor disagreement — fraud and judgement, not error.
tell: Intent is the dividing line.

rule: Counting and inspecting goods on receipt prevents paying for what never arrived.
trap: Authorisation, dual signatures and prenumbered checks — real controls, different risks.
tell: Match the control to the specific risk named.

rule: Pressure to hit internal targets, and preparing to qualify for financing.
trap: Complying with auditors or with Sarbanes-Oxley — reasons not to manipulate.
tell: Motive must be a pressure to overstate.

rule: No certain nonaudit services for audit clients; report to the audit committee, not management.
trap: Code-of-ethics enforcement and a five-year firm rotation, which the act does not require of firms.
tell: Independence is the theme.

rule: Management assesses internal control effectiveness and supports a stronger board and audit committee.
trap: Rotation and loan authorisation — those apply to auditors and are prohibited respectively.
tell: Management's duties, not the auditor's.

rule: They investigate fraud and review records and controls.
trap: Doing the original accounting, or issuing GAAP opinions — that is the external auditor.
tell: Internal auditors check work; they do not perform it or opine on it.

rule: It ensures users receive reliable information.
trap: Supporting auditors, boards or controllers — other bodies' roles.
tell: Protection of the investor is the mandate.

rule: Insight for management, and detailed data for internal decisions.
trap: Outside stakeholders and the IRS — those are financial and tax accounting.
tell: Internal audience, always.

rule: Management accounting is for internal planning, control and decision-making.
trap: Claims about being unbiased, financial-only, or not competitive — all describe financial accounting or are false.
tell: Who reads it decides the answer.

rule: Inventory appears for a manufacturer and not for a service firm.
trap: Cash, receivables and equipment, which both have.
tell: A service firm has nothing to hold in stock.

rule: A cost that changes as a result of the decision.
trap: Sunk, opportunity and out-of-pocket costs.
tell: Differential means it differs between alternatives.

rule: Selling and administrative expenses.
trap: Direct labour and manufacturing overhead — product costs.
tell: Product costs attach to inventory; period costs do not.

rule: A receptionist's salary and advertising are period costs.
trap: Wood and the craftsperson's salary — direct material and direct labour.
tell: Anything that touches the product is a product cost.

rule: They guide resolution of ethical dilemmas.
trap: Claims that standards prevent behaviour or predict character.
tell: A standard guides; it does not enforce or foresee.

rule: Direct materials plus direct labour plus manufacturing overhead.
trap: Totals that include selling or administrative costs.
tell: Include only what happens in the factory.

rule: Same computation, different figures.
trap: Totals that drop overhead or add a period cost.
tell: List the three product-cost buckets before adding.

rule: Direct labour and overhead are inventoried.
trap: Selling and legal costs.
tell: If it is not incurred to make the unit, it is not in inventory.

rule: Several highly differentiated products with varied overhead consumption.
trap: Single product lines, or similar products, where one rate is adequate.
tell: Diversity of products is what breaks traditional costing.

rule: Setup and material movement are batch-level.
trap: Unit, product-line and facility levels.
tell: Per batch, not per unit.

rule: Police cost is driven by the number of people present.
trap: Organiser hours, fees and insurance — costs, not drivers.
tell: A driver is what causes the cost to rise.

rule: Rate per activity times that product's activity consumption.
trap: Totals that use a single plant-wide rate.
tell: Each pool gets its own rate.

rule: Same method, different product.
trap: Numbers from the wrong pool or the wrong product.
tell: Track which pool and which product before multiplying.

rule: Rate times the actual driver volume.
trap: Products of the wrong two figures.
tell: Rate times base, and check both.

rule: If ABC shows a product costs more than traditional costing suggested, its price should rise.
trap: Lowering price, changing batch counts, or reverting to traditional costing.
tell: ABC revealed an undercosted product.

rule: Sales less variable costs, then less fixed costs, gives operating income.
trap: Totals that stop at contribution margin or drop a cost.
tell: Subtract variable first, then fixed.

rule: CVP studies profits across levels of activity.
trap: Liabilities and inventory — balance sheet items.
tell: Volume and profit are in the name.

rule: Total fixed cost stays the same; fixed cost per unit falls as volume rises.
trap: Both statements reversed, or per-unit fixed cost held constant.
tell: Total flat, per-unit falling. Always.

rule: Fixed costs divided by contribution margin per unit.
trap: Unit counts from dividing by price or by variable cost.
tell: Divide by the margin, not the price.

rule: Break-even units multiplied by price.
trap: Figures that use total cost or fixed cost alone.
tell: Revenue equals total cost at break-even.

rule: Read total cost off the total-cost line at the stated volume.
trap: Values read from the revenue line, or from the fixed-cost line.
tell: Identify which line before reading a number.

rule: Raising credit limits for all customers increases bad debt.
trap: Tightening policy, or discount terms, which reduce or do not raise risk.
tell: Which change lets weaker customers borrow more?

rule: Apply the collection percentages to each month's sales and sum what lands in the target month.
trap: Totals that apply the pattern to the wrong months.
tell: Build the collection schedule before adding.

rule: Apply the payment pattern across months.
trap: Totals from the wrong month's purchases.
tell: Which month is being paid, and for what.

rule: Sum the payments falling in the period under the stated terms.
trap: Totals that include or exclude a boundary month.
tell: Check the first and last month of the window.
